subject: MAP: technical gate — benchmark asks, owners, and target close
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@meddatahealth.com>, Evan Cole <evan.cole@meddatahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: technical gate — proposed benchmark asks & owners

Hi Asha / Evan — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed next step for the MAP technical milestone so we can align owners and a target close date.

Summary (from today)
- Goal: Validate model quality + unit economics for MedData’s clinical summarization flows at production scale.
- Primary success criteria: 1) Quality: pass 90% of the clinical QA prompt set (precision-focused acceptance — details below). 2) Latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 420ms for 2k token context when served from Redwood Dedicated in us-west region. 3) Unit cost: target <= $0.002 per 1k input tokens (inference-only).

Proposed model shortlist (initial):
- Llama-3-70B (fp16)
- Mistral-22B (q4f16 where applicable)
- RW-quant-13B (int8 candidate for cost testing)
- Ensemble fallback: Llama-3-7B for extremely low-latency use-cases

Who does what (proposed)
- MedData (Asha): provide 1) canonical evaluation prompt set (n ~ 600 prompts with annotations) and 2) a representative sample payload schema + avg token densities. Target delivery: 2026-10-28.
- Redwood (Jordan / Ben): provide benchmark harness, run initial latency/cost sweep on Dedicated, and deliver a short report (latency distributions, token-level cost, and failure modes). Target first run: 2026-11-04.
- MedData (Evan): share security checklist and minimum networking constraints for Dedicated/on-prem test options by 2026-10-25.
- Joint: agree on acceptance thresholds and gating logic (what constitutes a pass vs. require mitigation).

Timeline / target close
- Start: once MedData shares prompts and security constraints (see dates above).
- Target close for technical gate: 2026-11-18 (final decision to proceed to PO / pilot).

Attachments: map-technical-draft-20261021.pdf (draft MAP milestone), latency-benchmark-specs.csv (proposed metric defs)

Open questions for you:
1) Are the latency / cost targets in the ballpark? If they are too aggressive we can relax p95 or allow warm-cache assumptions.
2) Can you confirm the dataset size (approx rows / tokens) and whether PHI is sensitive (needs air-gapped test)?

Next steps: if this looks good I’ll drop a more formal MAP milestone doc into the Drive and schedule the first benchmark run with Ben.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Asha Reddy <asha.reddy@meddatahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@meddatahealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Oct 2026 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: technical gate — proposed benchmark asks & owners

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Dataset: we can share a de-identified sample of ~800 records (avg 3.2k tokens per record). We need confirmation that Redwood’s off-the-shelf evaluation harness can run on de-id data and we won’t need an air-gapped environment for the first run.
2) Security: we’ll send the security checklist, but two items to call out: explicit KMS integration required and audit logs for inference requests (retention 12 months).
3) Acceptance: the 90% QA pass feels reasonable as a starting point; we’ll land on the QA rubric together. For latency/cost, right now the product team is most sensitive to p95 and tail cost — if p95 > 600ms that will likely block.

Can Ben and Neha confirm if Dedicated runs can meet the p95 target for the 2k context? Also — will you include a cheap quantized candidate for a lower-cost baseline (we’d like a delta vs. high-quality fp16 runs).

We’ll get the prompt set to you by 10/28 and the security checklist by 10/25.

Thanks — Asha
Asha Reddy
Sr. Product Manager, Clinical Insights
Asha.Reddy@meddatahealth.com | +1 617-555-0114

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: technical gate — proposed benchmark asks & owners

Asha — perfect, thanks for the quick turn. Short answers:
- Dedicated feasibility: Ben has ok’d an initial Dedicated run — we’ll do both fp16 (higher-quality) and an int8 quantized pass (RW-quant-13B) so you get the delta on cost vs quality. Early expectation: fp16 p95 likely in the 350–500ms range for 2k context on a single-card Dedicated pod; int8 should pull p95 down and reduce cost 30–60% depending on batch/packing. We’ll report exact numbers with the first sweep.
- Security checklist: we can support KMS + audit logs. If you require air-gapped on-prem runs later we’ll scope separately (that will push timeline).

Actions I’ve updated on the MAP doc in Drive:
- MedData deliverables: prompt set (due 2026-10-28), security checklist (due 2026-10-25) — Asha/Evan
- Redwood deliverables: benchmark harness + initial run report (due 2026-11-04) — Ben
- Decision gate: 2026-11-18 — final technical acceptance

I’ve attached a small benchmark harness package and an updated latency spec. Ben — can you confirm when you can schedule the initial run? I’ll post a short calendar invite for the kickoff.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/MD-3472
Drive MAP folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMapTechPlaybook

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: MAP: technical gate — proposed benchmark asks & owners

Jordan / Neha — quick internal note and confirmation:
- I’ve reserved a Dedicated pod in us-west for the evening of 2026-11-03 to run the first sweep (fp16 and int8 candidates).
- I’ll run with the provided harness and the sample prompts once Asha drops them. Expected deliverables: 1) latency distribution .csv, 2) token-level cost estimate, 3) brief notes on failure modes and stability.
- Estimated cost for initial run (approx): $2,200 (one-time benchmarking run across three model variants). I’ll refine this after the first dry run.

Neha — I’ll need your help capturing the acceptance rubric in the report (QA pass definition + weightings) so the pass/fail is explicit in the MAP doc.

Onward — Ben
